results.title: Where Locals Eat Near Hongdae: A Homemade Korean Buffet in Hapjeong
results.content:
Restaurant: Montmartre Hill (몽마르뜨언덕)
 Address: 37 Jandari-ro 7-gil, Mapo-gu, Seoul, South Korea
 Nearest Station: Hapjeong Station, Exit 2
 Walking Distance: Approximately 4–5 minutes
 Food: Korean home-style buffet
 Dining Style: All-you-can-eat, pay after eating
 Price: ₩10,000 at the time of my visit
 Opening Hours: Lunch-focused operation. Please check the latest hours before visiting.

Find the restaurant: Google Maps | Naver Map [...] It’s the kind of neighborhood restaurant where local workers come for a familiar, filling lunch. The menu changes daily, the atmosphere is welcoming, and the buffet format lets you enjoy several different Korean dishes in one sitting.

I’d especially recommend it to travelers who want to try Korean home-style food beyond the usual barbecue, fried chicken, and street food.

And if you’re traveling alone, don’t worry. I found it comfortable for a solo lunch, too. [...] Go during lunchtime: This is a lunch-focused restaurant, so avoid arriving too close to closing time.
 Expect a changing menu: The main dishes and side dishes vary depending on the day.
 Start with small portions: You can always refill your plate, so there’s no need to take too much at once.
 Try the fresh vegetables with meat: Making your own Korean-style lettuce wrap is part of the fun.
 Solo dining is welcome: Smaller tables make it comfortable for people eating alone.

results.title: What to Eat in Seoul: 22 Must-Eat Spots (2026 Food Guide)
results.content:
During my days as an ESL teacher, we had a rotation of cheap lunch spots around my hagwon (private academy)—one for every day of the week.

Tuesday was always Kimbap Cheonguk (김밥천국) day, though we simply called it The Orange Place thanks to its cheerful, ubiquitous orange sign. The name actually means Kimbap Heaven. This franchise is a national treasure, offering no-nonsense Korean comfort food at prices that won’t dent your travel budget.
